comparison: Both evaluate Piezo1 expression in L cells (C1-C4). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with converging mRNA and immunofluorescence data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 criticizing immunofluorescence quality as having 'very high background and overall poor specificity' and requesting alternative validation methods like RNAscope.

Both evaluate HFD metabolic phenotype and Piezo1/Proglucagon correlations (C5-C10). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes correlational nature doesn't prove causation. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of 'solid' physiological characterization per editor.

Both evaluate human RYGB data (C11-C13). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes small sample size (n=6) and lack of mechanistic data. Peer reviewers do not specifically challenge these human correlative findings.

Both evaluate L-cell-specific knockout model generation and validation (C15-C21, C31-C36). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with sound genetic strategy. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 expressing major concerns about validation depth and stating 'Images in Fig 1e are not convincing for transduction of GFP in L-cells' with apparent off-target expression in muscle and submucosa.

Both evaluate metabolic phenotype of knockout mice (C22-C28, C49). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with comprehensive characterization. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN despite 'solid' physiological data, because Reviewer 2 identifies a critical confound: '>50% drop-off in GLP-1+ cells' suggesting altered L-cell density rather than direct Piezo1 function may explain the phenotype.

Both evaluate specificity controls showing knockout is intestinal-specific (C25-C26, C29-C30). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes comprehensive spatial characterization validates the model. Peer reviewers do not challenge these specificity data.

Both evaluate hormone-specific effects showing GLP-1 reduced but PYY/CCK unchanged (C37-C39). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes authors don't adequately explain selectivity. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 finding it 'curious' that GLP-1 and PYY are differentially affected despite co-expression in L cells and requesting mechanistic clarification.

Both evaluate tight junction protein data ruling out barrier dysfunction (C41-C42). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as important control. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 stating this is 'a suboptimal evaluation of barrier function' and insufficient to rule out epithelial integrity issues.

Both evaluate HFD phenotype persistence (C50-C57). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with consistency strengthening conclusions. Peer reviewers find SUPPORTED though inheriting the L-cell density confound concern from NCD results.

Both evaluate GLP-1 analog rescue experiments (C58-C62). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this demonstrates GLP-1 deficiency is causally related to phenotype. Peer reviewers accept these rescue data without challenge.

Both evaluate pharmacological activation with Yoda1 and antagonism with GsMTx4 (C63-C70). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes potential off-target effects but consistency with genetic data is reassuring. Peer reviewers do not challenge these gain-of-function experiments.

Both evaluate genetic epistasis showing Yoda1 requires L-cell Piezo1 (C71-C73). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this addresses off-target concerns and confirms specificity. Peer reviewers accept this as strengthening pharmacological specificity.

Both evaluate intestinal bead implantation experiments (C74-C80). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes lack of Piezo1-dependence testing is a significant gap. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 raising concerns about unclear mechanisms and confounding from 'intestinal obstruction and dysmotility' rather than pure mechanical stimulation.

Both evaluate primary L cell experiments with calcium imaging and Yoda1 (C81-C86). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting primary cells strengthen conclusions. Peer reviewers find SUPPORTED though Reviewer 1 notes 'limited amount of primary L cells' were used.

Both evaluate loss-of-function in primary L cells with shRNA (C87-C89). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, complementing gain-of-function studies. Peer reviewers find SUPPORTED as part of direct cellular evidence, though concerns about knockdown efficiency characterization remain.

Both evaluate ex vivo mechanical tension experiments (C90-C96). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes strong evidence for mechanotransduction but questions physiological relevance of tension protocol. Peer reviewers accept this as direct evidence without specific challenge.

Both evaluate STC-1 cell line patch-clamp and Yoda1 dose-response (C97-C104). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes strong mechanistic data but cell line limitations. Peer reviewers accept findings though Reviewer 1 expresses concern about relying 'mainly in the STC-1 cell line' rather than primary cells.

Both evaluate mechanical stretch in STC-1 cells (C105-C108). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval questions physiological relevance of stretch protocol. Peer reviewers do not specifically challenge these complementary mechanical stimulation data.

Both evaluate Piezo1 overexpression and knockdown in STC-1 cells (C109-C112). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes bidirectional approach is rigorous but questions overexpression levels and knockdown efficiency. Peer reviewers accept as complementary evidence.

Both evaluate CaMKKβ-CaMKIV-mTORC1 pathway manipulation (C113-C118). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes experiments don't directly link Piezo1 to pathway. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 stating 'data is not convincing' and requesting chemical inhibitors be tested in knockout mice or STC-1 cells to demonstrate Piezo1-dependence.

Both evaluate rapamycin blocking Piezo1-induced GLP-1 (C119-C120). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as linking Piezo1 to mTOR but notes rapamycin complexity. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 noting 'mechanisms of calcium signaling...and mTOR...remain unreconciled' and questioning pathway logic.

Both address the proposed CaMKKβ-CaMKIV-mTORC1 signaling mechanism (C48 in both, C43-C49 in OpenEval). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes evidence is associative rather than mechanistic. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN with editor stating 'Data to support the proposed mechanism were considered incomplete' and reviewers questioning the Ca2+/cAMP release pathway versus mTOR synthesis pathway logic and time course.

OpenEval provides comprehensive summary of all findings (C121-C137) and finds evidence SUPPORTED with convergence from multiple approaches, noting therapeutic potential is speculative but reasonable. No corresponding peer review summary evaluation found.
